item.content:encoded:
Updated Yankees projected Wild Card Series roster without Aaron Judge
NEW YORK - Here was the scenario these Yankees hoped to avoid, but couldn't - a triumphant Tampa Bay Rays team, celebrating their AL East title on Bronx turf.
"They've put together a fantastic regular season to earn that,'' said manager Aaron Boone, after the Rays' 6-1 victory in Tuesday's nightcap of a split doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
"Hopefully, we get another crack at them.''
That would be in a best-of-five AL Division Series, but only if the Yankees advance from a best-of-three Wild Card series, which they'll host - likely against the rival Red Sox.
With that Wild Card opponent in mind, here is our updated version of a Yankees 26-man playoff roster (12 pitchers, 14 position players), for a series that would begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
Rosters can be altered before each postseason round. Injured players can be replaced in-series (pitcher for pitcher, position player for position player) but the injured player is ineligible for the next playoff series.
Projected Yankees pitchers (12)
Starters (3): RHPs Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole; LHP Max Fried.
Relievers (9): RHPs David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Will Warren, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber; LHPs Ryan Weathers, Tim Hill, Brent Headrick, Carlos Rodon.
On the bubble: RHPs Clarke Schmidt.
Also available: RHPs Luis Gil, Elmer Rodriguez, Yerry de los Santos, Bradley Hanner, Carlos Lagrange; LHP Ryan Yarbrough.
Currently injured: RHPs Fernando Cruz, Angel Chivilli, Kervin Castro.
Analysis: Would the Yanks start anyone but Schlittler in Game 1?
Well, nothing's been firmly stated about the first round rotation, though Schlittler - the odds-on choice for the AL Cy Young Award - would be on normal rest for the opener.
Cole (Wednesday) and Schlittler (Thursday) will make their final regular season starts during this Rays series, though Boone mentioned limiting both starters in these tune-ups for postseason.
In the bullpen, Schmidt's recent bout of biceps cramping wasn't fully resolved as of Tuesday; he was due to be re-examined after a throwing session.
It's possible that even a slight setback takes Schmidt out of consideration for an important playoff spot, moving Michael Fulmer off the bubble and on the roster.
Rodon's eight shutout innings in Tuesday's doubleheader opener was his best effort, during an impressive stretch drive.
He'd be certain to start Game 1 or 2 of a Division Series vs. the Rays, but the Yanks might need his services - in some capacity - to advance vs. Boston, so he's now included here.
Projected Yankees infielders, utility/DH (9)
Infielders (7): Luis Garcia Jr., 1B; Paul Goldschmidt, 1B; Ben Rice, 1B-DH; Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B; George Lombard Jr., SS; Anthony Volpe, 2B-SS; Ryan McMahon, 3B.
Utility players: (2): Jose Caballero, IF-OF; Amed Rosario, 3B-2B.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Max Schuemann.
Analysis: Garcia and McMahon are slumping at the wrong time, while Chisholm - who just returned off the IL (right thumb sprain) on Tuesday - has this week to find his rhythm again at the plate.
But that trio of lefty hitters might all be starting on the bench against Boston, which could employ three lefty starters against the Yanks.
That puts Caballero in play as a third base option, with the veteran Goldschmidt (.997 OPS vs. lefties) at first base, the rookie Lombard at short, and Volpe recast as a second baseman.
Projected Yankees outfielders (3)
Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Jasson Dominguez.
Currently injured: Aaron Judge, Trent Grisham.
Analysis: That's a thin outfield without Judge, whom the Yanks are not planning to have for at least the Wild Card series - per Boone - due to the captain's "moderate'' right calf strain.
It's increasingly unlikely that Grisham (strained hamstring) is available, too, by next week, and that presents a danger considering Ramos' defensive deficiencies.
For that same reason, Dominguez is on the outside. Mostly, the Yanks need the potent right-handed bats of Ramos (who has found his hitting groove) and Rosario to combat Boston's lefty pitching.
Caballero could find himself pressed into outfield duty, too.
Without Judge, "it's going to be super tough on us,'' said Ramos. "But we're going to go forward, for sure.''
Yankees' projected catchers (2)
Austin Wells, Ali Sanchez.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: J.C. Escarra.
Analysis: Wells has been a better offensive presence after a brutal first half, and Sanchez has learned the staff and he earned much praise from Rodon for his contribution to Tuesday's game one win.
Boone has kept the Cole-Wells pairing together, and you'd still anticipate Wells getting starts vs. Boston's lefty starters throughout this opening series.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK – La noticia sobre el regreso de Aaron Judge a la lista de lesionados aún estaba fresca, habiendo sido anunciada menos de una hora antes, y ya Cody Bellinger estaba imaginando cómo los Yankees podían tener éxito en la postemporada sin su capitán.
Desafortunadamente para Judge y su club, han tenido mucha práctica haciendo exactamente eso esta temporada. No han tenido otra opción.
"Falta Judge y duele", dijo Bellinger. "Todos sabemos que él es el mejor bateador del juego. Para nosotros aquí, nuestra mentalidad es que vamos a tener que encontrar la manera. Creo que el talento en este clubhouse habla por sí mismo. Estoy completamente seguro de que tenemos suficiente talento aquí para salir, ganar y vencer a cualquiera.
Ahora tendrán su oportunidad para demostrarlo.
El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, confirmó el martes que Judge está lidiando con un esguince "moderado" de la pantorrilla derecha y no se espera que esté listo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas, que comenzaría el 29 de septiembre.
La disponibilidad de Judge para las rondas posteriores, especialmente la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana, también está en duda. Pero los Yankees necesitan llegar allí primero. Aquí hay cinco motivos por los que los Yankees, elogiados como favoritos para ganar el banderín, aún pueden llegar a la Serie Mundial incluso si Judge no regresa:
Lanzadores abridores dominantes
**
Cuando Carlos Rodón lanzó ocho entradas sin permitir carreras en la **victoria por 2-0 del martes sobre los Rays, no sólo mantuvo el champán en el clubhouse de Tampa Bay (por el momento), sino que también sirvió como un recordatorio de la mayor fortaleza de los Yankees.
Rodón podría ni siquiera abrir un partido en una posible Serie de Comodines, quedando detrás de los favoritos al premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole y Max Fried. En pocas palabras, la rotación los ha mantenido a flote.
Los abridores de los Yankees han permitido dos carreras limpias o menos en 40 de 51 aperturas desde el 28 de julio, incluyendo una carrera limpia o menos en 33 de esas aperturas, acumulando efectividad de 2.50 en ese período. En general, han permitido una carrera o menos en 65 encuentros, un récord de franquicia en una sola campaña.
"Venimos a ganar cada partido, sin importar quién esté en el terreno", dijo Rodón. "Obviamente, es difícil cuando no tienes al mejor jugador del mundo en el terreno contigo. Tengo la esperanza de que vuelva. Pero... se trata simplemente de ganar juegos para nosotros.
Hay otro trueno
Esto no es el 2022, cuando los 62 jonrones de Judge establecieron un récord de la Liga Americana para una sola temporada y sirvieron como el motor indiscutible de la ofensiva. Principalmente debido a la lesión en la costilla, Judge se limitó a un promedio de .241, 18 vuelacercas y 41 impulsadas en 66 encuentros. Ben Rice asumió gran parte de la carga este año, cumpliendo con la predicción de la primavera de Boone de 39 cuadrangulares.
Bellinger sigue siendo una fuerza impactante, mientras que el aumento de la velocidad del bate del dominicano Luis García Jr. sugiere que su producción es sostenible, a pesar de una reciente caída. Mientras tanto, el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha mostrado poder después de un comienzo lento y se confiará en él en los playoffs contra lanzadores zurdos.
"Sabemos que somos capaces de ganar partidos", dijo Boone, quien señaló el récord de 36-24 del club desde el descanso del Juego de las Estrellas, la mayor parte del cual ocurrió sin Judge. "Nos hemos tenido que enfrentar a jugar sin muchas piezas clave en diferentes momentos y durante grandes tramos de esta campaña”.
**Los jóvenes pueden dar la cara
**
El cubano-estadounidense George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones llamaron la atención durante la reciente serie del club contra los Diamondbacks, cuando dieron jonrones con un total combinado de 872 pies calculados por Statcast contra Corbin Burnes – potentes batazos de 424 y 448 pies, respectivamente, que sugieren que se están sintiendo más cómodos en Grandes Ligas.
Ha habido algunos obstáculos durante sus primeros meses de actividad en las Mayores, con Lombard cometiendo errores en seis compromisos consecutivos en un período y Jones mostrando los swings en blanco que probablemente siempre sean parte de su juego. Pero el talento es real y nadie debería sorprenderse si alguno de los novatos brilla en un gran momento de octubre.
"Realmente sólo tenemos que jugar uno para el otro; apoyarnos mutuamente, pasar la batuta", dijo Bellinger. "Haces tu trabajo y controlas lo que puedes”.
Mejorando la salud
Mientras la situación de Judge no está clara, los Yankees están volviendo lentamente a estar completos.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. fue activado de la lista de lesionados entre los juego de la doble-jornada del martes, restaurando una presencia dinámica. Ha sido un año decepcionante en general, pero Chisholm estaba en racha en el momento de su lesión (de 46-18, .391). Los Yankees esperarán que retome eso.
Mientras tanto, Anthony Volpe aprovechó al máximo una oportunidad ante la ausencia de Chisholm, lo que podría haberle valido un lugar en el roster de playoffs, especialmente si los Yankees optan por contar con 11 lanzadores y 15 jugadores de posición en la primera ronda. Se cree que Trent Grisham está en la contienda para el roster.
"Con suerte, más personas podrán unirse y hacernos más formidables en el camino", dijo Boone.
Un bullpen reforzado
Los relevistas de los Yankees han estado entre los mejores de Grandes Ligas todo el año, pero ha habido señales preocupantes últimamente. Brent Headrick ocupa el segundo lugar en las Grandes Ligas con 79 presentaciones y ha mostrado una velocidad inconsistente. Mientras tanto, David Bednar y Paul Blackburn siguen en buena forma.
Debido a que los Yankees no tendrían por qué para a tener cinco abridores en octubre, la ayuda está en camino. Will Warren tiene programada una última apertura y luego pasará a un rol de relevista, dando al bullpen una opción intrigante de múltiples entradas. Clarke Schmidt y Ryan Weathers también están en consideración.
"Eso es lo bueno de la postemporada; los muchachos caen en diferentes roles y muchas veces pueden ser heroicos en papeles que no necesariamente imaginabas al inicio de la temporada", expresó Boone.

item.content:encoded:
Fried (5-5) took the loss in the second game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Rays, giving up four runs on six hits and two walks over 6.2 innings. He struck out four.
The veteran lefty kept things close until the seventh inning, when Tampa Bay tagged Fried for three runs and chased him from the mound after 97 pitches (64 strikes). With the 6-1 loss, the Rays clinched the AL East crown, but the Yankees are still locked into a wild-card spot. Tuesday's outing was the first time Fried had allowed more than one run since July 27, and he wraps up his regular season with a 2.80 ERA, 0.99 WHIP and 104:33 K:BB in 112.2 innings. His next start should come in the first round of the playoffs, which will begin for New York next Tuesday, Sept. 29.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Aaron Boone Delivers Clear Max Fried Verdict Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Keith Watkins
item.description: The New York Yankees saw the Tampa Bay Rays claim the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night. A 6-1 loss in the nightcap of a doubleheader split ended whatever remained of the division chase and confirmed what had felt inevitable for weeks. The Yankees are headed to the Wild Card Series. The sting of the celebration was real. So was the pragmatism that followed it. With five regular season games remaining and the postseason less than a week away, manager Aaron Boone's focus has already
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees saw the Tampa Bay Rays claim the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night. A 6-1 loss in the nightcap of a doubleheader split ended whatever remained of the division chase and confirmed what had felt inevitable for weeks. The Yankees are headed to the Wild Card Series.
The sting of the celebration was real. So was the pragmatism that followed it. With five regular season games remaining and the postseason less than a week away, manager Aaron Boone's focus has already shifted to October.
His assessment of one pitcher in particular made that clear.
Boone's Comments on Fried
Max Fried will not pitch again in the regular season. Tuesday's start against the Rays was his final tuneup before the playoffs.
"I think he looks great," Boone said. "I thought he was really good tonight. He threw the ball well. His curveball was really, really good tonight. Cutter was there. For the most part, was filling up the strike zone really well."
Fried's night unraveled in the seventh when a bunt play went sideways and three runs came in. Before that, he had been efficient and sharp. Boone saw a pitcher who is ready for October, not one who got tagged for four runs.
"He managed contact really well. I thought he was efficient," Boone said. "He's in a good place ready to go. Looking forward to seeing him out there in the postseason now."
Managing the Final Five Games
With the standings locked in, Boone outlined how the Yankees will approach the rest of the week. The priority is keeping players sharp without wearing anyone down.
"Getting guys ready, picking some days for some guys to get off," Boone said. "We're the real game. So we're playing. But I will pick some spots to get some guys down."
Cody Bellinger and Austin Wells are candidates for rest days. Spencer Jones may get a day to manage. Boone also mentioned experimenting with defensive positions and being selective about when leverage relievers pitch.
The balance is delicate. The games do not matter in the standings. The rhythm and preparation matter for everything that comes after.
Final Word for the Yankees
The division belongs to Tampa Bay. The Yankees know it. They watched the celebration and walked off their own field.
What happens next is the only thing that counts. Fried is ready. Cole and Schlittler are lined up. The rotation has three arms capable of winning a postseason start.
The Wild Card Series begins next week, with a Red Sox series in the Bronx the most likely outcome. Boone's message on Tuesday was simple. His team is not done. The pitching is in place. Now it is time to prove it matters.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees' Aaron Boone Delivers Clear Max Fried Verdict Before Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees got their Carlos Rodon answer even as the AL East slipped away
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Against Tampa Bay, Carlos Rodon gave the Yankees eight scoreless innings with eight strikeouts. That was about as much as a starter can give them against the team that has been keeping them out of first place. They beat Tampa Bay 2-0 in the first game of Tuesday’s doubleheader. A few hours later, the Rays won 6-1 and clinched the AL East in the Bronx. Both results matter. Rodon’s start showed what this rotation can do in a playoff game; the loss showed why one excellent arm won’t settle the rest
item.content:encoded:
Against Tampa Bay, Carlos Rodon gave the Yankees eight scoreless innings with eight strikeouts. That was about as much as a starter can give them against the team that has been keeping them out of first place.
They beat Tampa Bay 2-0 in the first game of Tuesday’s doubleheader. A few hours later, the Rays won 6-1 and clinched the AL East in the Bronx. Both results matter. Rodon’s start showed what this rotation can do in a playoff game; the loss showed why one excellent arm won’t settle the rest of the Yankees’ problems.
There was nothing cheap about those eight innings. Rodon kept Tampa Bay off the board long enough for Cody Bellinger’s two-run homer to stand as the entire margin. David Bednar handled the ninth. For a staff that has spent the year sorting through injuries and changing roles, that is a useful October blueprint.
The Yankees have a real decision behind their ace
Rodon’s 2.67 ERA after the first game is strong enough to make his postseason role a serious conversation. Cam Schlittler has earned the ace label, and Max Fried is still part of the picture. The question is how the Yankees order those starts and what they ask from each pitcher if the Wild Card Series arrives on schedule.
Clarke Schmidt’s return makes that decision more crowded. The rotation questions are already on the table, and Rodon just made his case with the most useful kind of outing: a long one against a division rival.
Rodon also saved the bullpen in the opener. That gets lost when the second game ends with a division celebration in the other clubhouse, but it matters if the Yankees have to play three high-pressure games in five days.
The AL East result still stings
The Yankees are in the postseason. The division title and its first-round bye belong to Tampa Bay, though, and Tuesday made the gap feel obvious. New York scored three runs in two games while its pitchers needed to be close to perfect just to force a split.
Rodon’s outing belongs in any serious October plan. It cannot cover for another quiet night from the lineup. The Yankees got a strong answer from one starter and a reminder that their hitters have less room for silence now.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] What should the Yankees do with Carlos Rodón?
item.dc:creator: Jake Devin
item.description: Leading off yesterday's doubleheader, Carlos Rodón pitched like a man who had something to prove. In a way, he does. He may be asked to step aside if the club needs a three-man rotation for a potential Wild Card series next week, widely viewed as the fourth guy sitting outside the Yankees' Big 3 in their rotation, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, and Gerrit Cole. Rodón's also had to answer doubts all year as he's dealt with numerous injuries, starting the season on the IL after offseason elbow surgery
item.content:encoded:
Leading off yesterday's doubleheader, Carlos Rodón pitched like a man who had something to prove. In a way, he does. He may be asked to step aside if the club needs a three-man rotation for a potential Wild Card series next week, widely viewed as the fourth guy sitting outside the Yankees' Big 3 in their rotation, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, and Gerrit Cole. Rodón's also had to answer doubts all year as he's dealt with numerous injuries, starting the season on the IL after offseason elbow surgery and a hamstring injury in spring training, before hitting the IL again with elbow inflammation over the summer. He's been nails through it all, posting a 2.67 ERA in 16 starts, saving his best for last in the form of an eight-inning masterpiece Tuesday afternoon.
Rodón's performance forces some interesting questions for the Yankees, particularly when it comes to their strategy should they face the Red Sox in a best-of-three. How should the Yankees deploy Rodón next week?
First off, you can make a compelling argument that they should just start the man. By any measure, he's been the club's third-best starter this season, behind Schlittler and Fried and ahead of Cole. Cole has been more durable throughout the season, but Rodón's been in better form down the stretch, posting a 1.89 ERA in seven starts since coming off the IL a second time. Why not just roll with the hot hand?
The Yankees seem likely to go with Cole, preferring to defer to both Cole's extensive track record and status over Rodón's superior recent performance, a decision that's both debatable and reasonable. Should that be their move, the strategic implications run deeper.
They could use Rodón in something of a piggyback role, letting him eat multiple innings in support of one of their top starters (perhaps Cole, the team's shakiest starter lately?). They could let him air it out in a one-inning relief role for one series, or even deploy him as a lefty specialist, choosing to bring him in if and when the opposing lineup presents a lane of left-handed hitters.
It's not at all a simple decision, in no small part because there's another plausible idea here: keep him in reserve for a potential ALDS. If the Yankees burn all four of their top starters in some fashion in the ALWC, they'd be forced to start Will Warren in Game 1 of the ALDS should they advance. The difference between Rodón and Warren isn't exactly massive, and Warren has been strong down the stretch as well, but saving Rodón for the ALDS allows the Yankees to ensure that every game is started by one of their top four pitchers.
It's a complicated calculus; every tactical decision you make in one postseason game or series has major strategic consequences on every future game and series. Rodón could be an extra relief weapon in a Wild Card series, he could be held in reserve for a future series, and you could even argue he should just start against Boston. What do you think? What should the Yankees do with Rodón?
On the site this morning, Matt reviews Tuesday night's American League action, and John ruminates on Moneyball, the movie, released on this day 15 years ago. Later, Jonathan's entry in our Yankees Birthday series features a fan favorite from a bygone era, Joba Chamberlain, and Josh discusses Aaron Judge's calf injury, and the Yankees' continued reluctance to be forthright whenever Judge gets hurt.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] What Carlos Rodon gem does for Yankees’ postseason rotation
item.dc:creator: Randy Miller
item.description: NEW YORK — The Yankees went into Tuesday's day-night doubleheader hoping to make a last stand with the division title all but lost. One Rays win in four games this week at Yankee Stadium and the Yankees would be locked into a best-of-three Wild Card Series. They lasted until Game 2, a 6-1 Rays win that clinched the AL East. The Yankees' Carlos Rodon-fueled 2-0 win in Game 1 guaranteed they'd be home for the first round. Two more Red Sox wins will ensure a repeat of last October's first-round mat
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — The Yankees went into Tuesday's day-night doubleheader hoping to make a last stand with the division title all but lost.
One Rays win in four games this week at Yankee Stadium and the Yankees would be locked into a best-of-three Wild Card Series.
They lasted until Game 2, a 6-1 Rays win that clinched the AL East.
The Yankees' Carlos Rodon-fueled 2-0 win in Game 1 guaranteed they'd be home for the first round. Two more Red Sox wins will ensure a repeat of last October's first-round matchup that the Yankees won in three games.
You remember Game 3, right?
That was Cam Schlittler's real coming out party. That's when the tall rookie right-hander showed everyone how great he can be throwing up eight shutout innings with 12 strikeouts and no walks in a do-or-die game.
That's the Schlittler that the Yankees have seen in almost all of his 2026 starts. He's been so good that he's a lock to win the AL Cy Young and he's getting MVP consideration, too.
As for who starts Game 1 of the Yankees' Wild Card Series next Tuesday, they could go Schlittler on regular rest or Gerrit Cole on extra rest.
It doesn't matter though because none of the Yankees' Wild Card Series starting pitchers will be able to start two games in the next round.
The Wild Card Series starts Sept. 29, and the two American League Division Series begin four days later on Oct. 3. So, unless the Yankees opt to use a starter on short rest — and they won't — their third or fourth starter will get the nod for Game 1 of the ALDS if the Yankees advance.
Another option would be Schlittler in Game 1, Max Fried in Game 2 and Cole in Game 3.
The big lefty could be a long relief option for the Red Sox … or saved for two starts against the Rays.
If the Yankees win their Wild Card Series, the Rays would be up next for a best of five that starts at Tropicana Field.
Rodon manhandled the Rays in Tuesday's opener, eight shutout innings, two singles, eight strikeouts and no walks. After this outing, who better to line up for Game 1 and Game 5 than Rodon if Schlittler isn't rested?
What's next for Rodon?
TBD.
Manager Aaron Boone said the plan is to skip Rodon on Sunday and then figure out what's next.
"Ah, we haven't got that far yet," the skipper said after Tuesday's first game.
That made sense until the Rays clinched.
If the Yankees had been alive in the division race heading into Sunday, Rodon is lined up to pitch game 162.
The Yankees love what they're getting from Rodon, who hasn't allowed more than three runs for 26 consecutive starts (although he did have a three-run, six-inning dud against the Blue Jays in Game 3 of a Division Series last October).
Two injured list stints wiped out more than half of Rodon's season, which is year four of a six-year, $162 million pact - but he's consistently been good to great when he's been pitching and he was as good as he's ever been as a Yankee in Tuesday's opener. He set a tone setting down the stars in the Rays' lineup 1-2-3 in the first inning – Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda by strikeout, Junior Caminero on a lineout – then put up seven more zeroes.
The Rays managed two baserunners in eight innings facing Rodon, both singles. The lefty's last strikeout was special, No. 1,500 over an injury-riddled career that's included three All-Star selections, a no-hitter for the White Sox and 18 wins last year.
"His stuff is really good, especially today with the heater and the profile of that fastball," Boone said. "I think in a lot of ways his fastball is in a better place than it was last year, which was a great season for him. But we've seen over the last couple years him really develop as a pitcher and develop the secondary (pitches).
"When he came to us, his calling card throughout his career was just overpowering fastball/slider combo. The changeup the last couple years has become an excellent pitch for him. So he can pitch now. He can beat you different ways. But I like where his fastball is right now."
The Yankees' starting pitching has been the best in the majors this year, and it's had to with Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton out of the lineup for much of the season. Tuesday's news that Judge is doubtful for the first round — maybe for the entire postseason — only adds to the pressure on the pitching staff.
If the Yankees aren't bounced in the first round, Rodon probably will get at least one and maybe two more shots at the Rays.
"I expect him to play a big role for us hopefully, especially if we go on a deep run in the postseason," Boone said. "I like where he's at right now."

item.title: [mlb.com] 5 reasons the Yankees can win without Judge
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch
item.description: NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain. Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice. “Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re g
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain.
Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice.
“Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here to go out, win and beat anybody.”
Now they’ll have their chance to prove it.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday that Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain of his right calf and is not expected to be ready for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which would begin on Sept. 29.
Judge’s availability for subsequent rounds, especially the AL Division Series, is also in doubt. But the Yankees need to get there first. Here are five reasons why the Yankees, lauded as pennant favorites, still can reach the Fall Classic even if Judge doesn’t return:
Dominant starting pitching
Rodón might not even draw a start in a potential Wild Card Series, standing in line behind AL Cy Young Award frontrunner Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried. Simply put, the rotation has kept them afloat.
Yankees starters have permitted two earned runs or fewer in 40 of 51 starts since July 28, including one earned run or fewer in 33 of those starts, compiling a 2.50 ERA over that span. Overall, they’ve allowed one run or fewer in 65 games, a single-season franchise record.
“We come to win every game, regardless of who is on the field,” Rodón said. “Obviously it’s tough when you don’t have the best player in the world on the field with you. I’m hopeful that he’ll be back. But … it’s just about winning games for us.”
There’s other thump
This isn’t 2022, when Judge’s 62 home runs set a single-season AL record and served as the unquestioned engine of the offense. Mostly because of the rib injury, Judge was limited to a .241 average, 18 homers and 41 RBIs across 66 games. Ben Rice shouldered much of the load, fulfilling Boone’s spring prediction of 39 homers.
Bellinger remains an impactful force, while Luis García Jr.’s increased bat speed suggests his production is sustainable despite a recent slump. Meanwhile, Heliot Ramos has shown power after a sluggish start and will be leaned upon in the playoffs against left-handed pitching.
“We know we’re capable of winning games,” said Boone, who noted the club’s 36-24 record since the All-Star break, most of which occurred without Judge. “We’ve had to play without a lot of key pieces at different points and for large chunks of this season.”
The kids are all right
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones opened eyes during the club’s recent series against the Diamondbacks, when they crushed a Statcast-calculated combined 872 feet of home runs against Corbin Burnes – big-boy blasts of 424 and 448 feet, respectively, that suggested they’re growing more comfortable in The Show.
There have been growing pains across their first months of big league activity, with Lombard committing errors in six consecutive games over one span and Jones showing the swing-and-miss that will probably always be part of his game. But the talent is real, and no one should be surprised if either rookie delivers in a big October moment.
“We really just have to play for each other; lean on each other, pass the baton,” Bellinger said. “You do your job and control what you can.”
Improving health
While Judge’s outlook is cloudy, the Yankees are slowly becoming more whole.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. was activated from the injured list between games of Tuesday’s doubleheader, restoring a dynamic presence. It has been a disappointing year overall, but Chisholm was hot at the time of his injury (18-for-46, .391). The Yanks will look for him to pick up where he left off.
Meanwhile, Anthony Volpe made the most of an opportunity in Chisholm’s absence, which could have earned him a spot on a playoff roster – especially if they go with 11 pitchers and 15 position players in the first round. Trent Grisham is thought to be in play for the playoff roster.
“Hopefully more people are able to join and make us more formidable along the way,” Boone said.
A bolstered bullpen
The Yankees’ relievers have been among the league’s best all year, but there have been concerning signs of late. Brent Headrick ranks second in the Majors with 79 appearances and has seen inconsistent velocity, for example, suggesting he could benefit from a breather once the AL East is decided. David Bednar and Paul Blackburn, meanwhile, remain sharp.
Because the Yankees would have no reason to roster five starting pitchers in October, help is on the way. Will Warren is scheduled to make one more start and then transition to a relief role, giving the ’pen an intriguing multi-inning option. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are also in the mix.
“That’s the beauty of the postseason; guys fall into different roles and a lot of times can become heroic in roles you didn’t necessarily count on at the start of the season,” Boone said.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Yankees preview postseason blueprint in doubleheader vs. Rays
item.dc:creator: James O'Connell
item.description: During a long day of baseball in the Bronx, the Yankees and Rays both took one game apiece in the day-night doubleheader between the top two teams in the American League — and teams that are on a collision course as potential ALDS opponents. It may have been a sneak peek of what’s to come, from the teams on the field to the chill in the air, and even what to expect from the club known as the Bronx Bombers. The Yankees have been, to put it kindly, offensively challenged in the absence of Aaron Ju
item.content:encoded:
During a long day of baseball in the Bronx, the Yankees and Rays both took one game apiece in the day-night doubleheader between the top two teams in the American League — and teams that are on a collision course as potential ALDS opponents.
It may have been a sneak peek of what’s to come, from the teams on the field to the chill in the air, and even what to expect from the club known as the Bronx Bombers.
The Yankees have been, to put it kindly, offensively challenged in the absence of Aaron Judge and with their captain likely to miss the Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. That’s not expected to change, as evidenced by their abysmal offensive performance on Tuesday.
The pinstripes scored three runs between the two games and totaled just eight hits. Their first hit in the nightcap didn’t come until the 7th inning.
However, the Yanks did show their strength and it came from their pair of southpaws on the mound. Carlos Rodon tossed eight shutout innings — where he reached 98 mph on his four-seamer and struck out eight batters — and Max Fried, who was superb for most of his outing, added 6.2 innings of four-run ball (three of which came in the seventh).
If the Yankees have an extended stay in October, the games will likely look a lot like they did for most of Tuesday.
Quick and quiet. Because if things start to get loud, chances are they aren’t the ones making the noise.
The Bombers are entering this postseason with pitching at the forefront of their identity, having horses such as Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and the pair of lefties who toed the slab against the Rays.
It’s an elite group to rely on, as the club owned the best ERA in baseball amongst starters with a 3.24. However, here’s a lot riding on each of those guys to be virtually perfect, as, barring a sudden change in offensive firepower, there won’t be many runs to come by.
Since May 31 — the game Judge last played before his rib injury kept him out until Sept. 8 — the Yankees rank 23rd in runs scored, 29th in batting average and 26th in WRC+. It’s not a recipe for success, and they have no choice but to make it work.
Hits like Cody Bellinger’s two-run homer in the day game may have to be enough to get the job done as Aaron Boone’s club showed you on Tuesday how they plan to compete and bring their 28th championship home this season.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Rays clinch AL East, celebrate after Yankees secure home field advantage for Wild Card round
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips

Alas, the second-place Bombers, burdened by injuries all season, officially missed out on a division title for the second straight season, as Tampa Bay clinched the American League East and a postseason bye with a 6-1 win in the second game of Tuesday’s doubleheader between the two teams. With their significantly richer rivals thwa
item.content:encoded:
When the Yankees retained a large chunk of their 2025 roster, they didn’t think they’d end up starting the 2026 playoffs in the same position that they did last year.
Alas, the second-place Bombers, burdened by injuries all season, officially missed out on a division title for the second straight season, as Tampa Bay clinched the American League East and a postseason bye with a 6-1 win in the second game of Tuesday’s doubleheader between the two teams. With their significantly richer rivals thwarted — the Yankees’ luxury tax payroll is $228.9 million more than Tampa’s, per Cot’s Contracts — the Rays excitedly shook hands in front of the Bronx faithful before popping bottles and lighting cigars in the visitor’s clubhouse at Yankee Stadium.
“It’s not a good feeling, for sure,” Yankees outfielder Heliot Ramos said after going 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.
“You don’t want anyone to be celebrating at your stadium,” added Max Fried, who allowed four earned runs over 6.2 innings.
It was a sour ending to a long day that began with a 2-0 victory for the Yankees, who are now 90-67 and six games behind the Rays with five games left in the regular season. That afternoon win ensured that the Yankees will have home field advantage in the Wild Card round, which begins on Sept. 29.
The likeliest scenario is that the Yankees will host the Red Sox, just as they did in last year’s Wild Card round.
The Yankees already knew that winning the division was an uphill battle coming into this four-game series against the Rays, as they needed to sweep just to keep that improbable dream alive after losing two games in Arizona over the weekend. And even with their win in Game 1 on Tuesday, the pinstripers only had a 1.8% chance of claiming the AL East, according to FanGraphs.
“You gotta give them credit,” Aaron Boone said of the 96-61 Rays on Tuesday morning. “They’ve won a ton of games this year, games that have probably been up in the air late, and they’ve come out on top. So they’ve had a great year, and they’re always a challenge to play.”
Drew Rasmussen was particularly challenging on Tuesday night, as he out-pitched Fried and didn’t permit a hit until Ramos led off the seventh inning with a double. The right-handed Rasmussen also struck out 11 while allowing one run over 6.2 innings.
With the division race over, the Yankees can now take the remainder of the week to rest key players and experiment before their likely rematch with Boston in the Wild Card round, which they expect to play without the injured Aaron Judge. If they can win that series, they’ll face the Rays again in the ALDS, a possibility that both clubs’ managers acknowledged on Tuesday night.
“This four-game series has been circled on both of our schedules for quite some time, and that’s because of so much respect that you have for the opponent,” Rays skipper Kevin Cash said. “That’s a very talented team, and we know that we could be seeing them here in another 10, 12 games.”
“Hopefully we get another crack at them in the next couple weeks,” Boone chimed in.
While the Yankees beat the Red Sox last October and won this year’s season series against them, the Wild Card round is not how they envisioned beginning the 2026 postseason after they fell short of a division title last year.
In 2025, the Yankees ended the regular season with the same record as the pennant-winning Blue Jays. However, Toronto won the season series tiebreaker between the two teams — and therefore the AL East — earned a bye in the playoffs, and defeated the Yankees in a four-game ALDS.
The Yankees last won the East in 2024. They lost that year’s World Series to the Dodgers.
The Yanks have won their division just three times since 2013, and they haven’t won a championship since 2009. However, they still believe they can end that drought after failing to secure an AL East crown.
“It kind of sucks,” Jazz Chisholm Jr. said of losing the division. “That’s what we work on all season, but it’s not the end goal for us. That end goal is the World Series, so it doesn’t really affect us here.”

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Drew Rasmussen allowed his only hit in the seventh inning and struck out 11 as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the New York Yankees 6-1 on Tuesday in the second game of a day-night doubleheader to clinch their fifth AL East title.
The Rays (96-61) secured home-field advantage throughout the American League playoffs and took their first division crown since 2021, when they won 100 games. Tampa Bay also earned AL East championships in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when the team had its first winning season after entering the league as an expansion franchise in 1998.
Yandy Díaz hit two-run single off reliever John Schreiber in the seventh and had another two-run single in the ninth for his AL-leading 175th hit. Tampa Bay opened a six-game lead over the second-place Yankees (90-67) with five to play.
In the opener, Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings as New York delayed Tampa Bay's division celebration with a 2-0 victory.
Taylor Walls started the three-run seventh with a bunt single against Max Fried (5-5) when first base was left uncovered. Ryan Vilade hit an RBI groundout in the third after Díaz’s flyball moved runners to second and third.
Rasmussen (16-5) was nine outs from joining Matt Garza as Tampa Bay pitchers with a no-hitter when he gave up a leadoff double to Heliot Ramos on his 97th pitch. Garza held the Detroit Tigers hitless at Tropicana Field on July 26, 2010.
After allowing Ramos’ hit to left field, Rasmussen got the next two outs before walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a full count. Kevin Kelly entered and permitted rookie George Lombard Jr.’s RBI single before retiring Austin Wells on a groundout.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches, 72 for strikes. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of 24 hitters and notched his fourth career double-digit strikeout game.
Rasmussen allowed one hit for the fourth time this year. He also yielded just one hit in six innings against the Yankees on April 12.
Cam Booser and Bryan Baker pitched an inning apiece to finish the three-hitter.
Fried allowed four runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings.
The Yankees were held to three hits or fewer for the 13th time this year.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38 ERA) opposes New York RHP Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63) on Wednesday night.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Larry Fleisher, The Associated Press

Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 08:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the AL East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays (96-61) won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games.
Tampa Bay also claimed division titles in the pandemic shortened 2020 season, 2010 and 2008 and will head to the postseason as the top seed in the AL.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches and struck out New York leadoff hitter Ben Rice twice. He also struck out rookie Spencer Jones to end the fourth after allowing a walk to Cody Bellinger, who he fanned in the first inning.
The right-hander exited after walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Kelly retired Austin Wells following Lombard's hit.
Yandy Diaz drove in two runs with a single in the seventh off reliever John Schreiber. Diaz added another two-run single in the ninth. The Rays scored their first run in the third when Ryan Vilade grounded out against New York's Max Fried (5-5), scoring Taylor Walls.
Cam Booser pitched a 1-2-3 eighth and Bryan Baker put two on in the ninth before retiring Lombard to secure the division crown.
Fried allowed four runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings. The left-hander struck out four, walked two and notched 10 ground ball outs.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [fingerlakes1.com] Yankees fall to Rays in Game 2 of doubleheader as Tampa Bay clinches AL East title | Fingerlakes1.com
item.dc:creator: Facebook Com; Fingerlakes1; Kyle Evans
item.description: The New York Yankees’ American League East hopes came to an end Tuesday night as the Tampa Bay Rays defeated New York 6-1 in Game 2 of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. The Yankees won the opening game 2-0 behind eight scoreless innings from Carlos Rodón, but Tampa Bay responded in the nightcap to clinch the division and the American League’s top playoff seed. New York managed just three hits against a Tampa Bay pitching staff that followed up its Game 1 loss with a dominant performance from Dre
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees’ American League East hopes came to an end Tuesday night as the Tampa Bay Rays defeated New York 6-1 in Game 2 of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
The Yankees won the opening game 2-0 behind eight scoreless innings from Carlos Rodón, but Tampa Bay responded in the nightcap to clinch the division and the American League’s top playoff seed.
New York managed just three hits against a Tampa Bay pitching staff that followed up its Game 1 loss with a dominant performance from Drew Rasmussen. The right-hander carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning before Heliot Ramos opened the frame with a double.
Rasmussen exited after Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked with two outs. George Lombard Jr. then delivered New York’s only run with a single that scored Ramos. Rasmussen finished with one run allowed on one hit and three walks over 6.2 innings while striking out 11.
Max Fried kept the Yankees within striking distance before Tampa Bay pulled away. Ryan Vilade’s groundout gave the Rays a 1-0 lead in the third inning.
Tampa Bay added three runs in the seventh. Taylor Walls drove in Chandler Simpson with a bunt single before Yandy Díaz followed with a two-run single. Walls also scored on the play after a close call at home plate was upheld following a Yankees challenge.
Fried allowed four runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four.
The Rays added two more runs in the ninth against Ryan Yarbrough and Michael Fulmer, with Díaz delivering another two-run single.
Chisholm, activated before Game 2 after missing 12 games with a sprained right thumb, went 1-for-3 with a walk and a strikeout.
The Yankees continue their series against Tampa Bay Wednesday at 7:05 p.m. Gerrit Cole is scheduled to start against Ian Seymour.

item.description:
The Yankees will not accomplish the chief goal of their regular season, which will make their chief goal of the postseason harder to accomplish. That Aaron Boone’s group will have to play a best-of-three series in the wild-card round — almost certainly against the Red Sox in The Bronx and almost certainly without Aaron Judge — is discouraging for a club that sought to avoid the same precarious position that it encountered last season.
Access the Yankees beat like never before
item.content:encoded:
The Yankees will not accomplish the chief goal of their regular season, which will make their chief goal of the postseason harder to accomplish.
That Aaron Boone’s group will have to play a best-of-three series in the wild-card round — almost certainly against the Red Sox in The Bronx and almost certainly without Aaron Judge — is discouraging for a club that sought to avoid the same precarious position that it encountered last season.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
That Boone’s group was forced to watch the Rays clinch — and celebrate the AL East title that the Yankees made it their mission to win — on The Bronx grass sure must have added some irritation and maybe some motivation.
One year later, the Yankees will enter the postseason the same way: through the dreaded back door that adds to their World Series degree of difficulty.
The Rays celebrated a 6-1 nightcap victory and division title on Tuesday night at the Stadium, where a 2-0 Yankees matinee win simply delayed the inevitable.
In Game 157, Tampa Bay (96-61) won its first AL East championship since 2021, and the Yankees (90-67) wrapped up the top wild card for a second consecutive season.
- CHECK OUT THE LATEST MLB STANDINGS AND YANKEES STATS
After Bryan Baker induced a ground out from George Lombard Jr. to end it, Baker raised his arms in triumph and the Rays began congratulating one another while the Yankees quietly shuffled out of their own dugout.
Last year it was the Blue Jays who edged out the Yankees (through a tiebreaker), forcing Boone’s crew to sweat out a three-game set against Boston before wilting against that Toronto club, which could arrange its starting pitchers and had home-field advantage.
And so the Yankees were vocal all spring and all season that this year, they expected better.
But amid a campaign with too many lulls, too many notable injuries and not enough step-ups during those injuries, they will enter October in the same position: likely fighting the Red Sox for a chance at knocking off AL East champions that they could not solve in the regular season.
The small-market, penny-pinching Rays did not steal the division but won it decisively.
The Yankees had been playing catch-up since June 28 and never caught up. With two more now meaningless games to play, the Rays have won seven of the 11 head-to-head matchups.
For a brief glimpse at what has gone wrong this season for the Yankees, consider how they lost the nightcap:
— A team that has not hit enough without Judge again did not hit enough without Judge, no-hit until the seventh inning against Drew Rasmussen. Heliot Ramos’ double ensured the night might be embarrassing but would not be humiliating.
— A team that did not capitalize enough on its excellent starting pitching again did not capitalize enough on its excellent starting pitching. They won the opener behind eight shutdown innings from Carlos Rodón, but a slip from Max Fried in the second game was the only opening Tampa required.
Shop Yankees Merch
All it took in the third inning was an infield single, a walk, a flyout that advanced both runners and a ground out that scored the go-ahead run. The deficit would grow in the seventh because …
— A team that did not play enough clean baseball again did not play enough clean baseball. With runners on first and third and one out, Taylor Walls pushed a bunt toward first base. Fried pounced, did not believe he had a play on Chandler Simpson at home and so he looked toward first, where no one covered. First baseman Luis García Jr. had charged, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. lingered around second base.
No out was recorded in what became a three-run frame that became one more regrettable inning in a season in which the Yankees have had too many to earn a first-round bye.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Carlos Rodón strengthens case for Yankees playoff rotation shuffle in dominant outing vs. Rays
item.dc:creator: Colin Keane
item.description: As the New York Yankees look ahead to the postseason, they have some big questions about their starting rotation. Trouble has been brewing of late when it comes to the reliability of Gerrit Cole. Carlos Rodón, who recently suffered a dip in velocity, didn't look like the best version of himself the last time through the rotation, either. Rodón has been good overall in his last few starts, but Yankees fans were still looking for more certainty entering Tuesday. As such, the first leg of Tuesday's
item.content:encoded:
As the New York Yankees look ahead to the postseason, they have some big questions about their starting rotation. Trouble has been brewing of late when it comes to the reliability of Gerrit Cole. Carlos Rodón, who recently suffered a dip in velocity, didn't look like the best version of himself the last time through the rotation, either. Rodón has been good overall in his last few starts, but Yankees fans were still looking for more certainty entering Tuesday.
As such, the first leg of Tuesday's double-header against the Tampa Bay Rays -- which Rodón started -- gave the veteran left-hander an opportunity to perform admirably and give the Yankees and their fanbase some peace of mind. And that's exactly what Rodón did.
Carlos Rodón just turned in a stellar start against the Rays as the postseason sits around the corner
If this is the version of Rodón that'll show up in October, the Yankees can't leave him out of their postseason plans. Rodón threw eight scoreless innings against the AL East-leading Rays, tallying eight strikeouts and allowing just three hits (all singles). He also didn't walk a soul. It was a statement performance that had Yankee Stadium buzzing.
It was a also a start for full of statistical milestones for Rodón. The win marked the 100th of his career, and Rodón also reached 1,500 career strikeouts with a slider in the eighth inning that had Jonny DeLuca looking helpless.
Rodón's excellence on Tuesday passed the eye test. His fastball was sharp and accurate. He was throwing first-pitch strikes on the regular, and he got into a rhythm in which he retired 10 batters in a row at one point.
Perhaps Rodón is kicking into high gear at the perfect time. His 2026 debut was delayed due to elbow surgery, and then inflammation cost him more time. But despite the concerning dip in velocity of late, Rodón has been really good since mid-August when you zoom out: 3-1 with a 1.89 ERA over his last seven starts.
The Yankees might need to consider Carlos Rodón for the ALWC
New York obviously hasn't announced its plan for the AL Wild Card Series, but it's beginning to feel like Rodón will be in consideration for one of the three games of the expected series battle against the Boston Red Sox.
While Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are all but likely locked in for two of the games, might the Yankees choose Rodón over Cole for the third? If he's looking like this (and with Cole looking subpar), it's a conversation. Boone has hinted that Cole will get a start, but he might need to change his thinking after today. Rodón at the moment looks like a hot hand that the Yankees can ride into the ALDS.

Rays' Drew Rasmussen loses no-hit bid in 7th inning on leadoff double by Heliot Ramos
NEW YORK (AP) — Tampa Bay right-hander Drew Rasmussen lost a no-hit bid against the New York Yankees on Tuesday night when Heliot Ramos led off the seventh inning with a double.
The Rays, attempting to clinch the AL East title, had a 4-0 lead when Ramos lined a 1-2 sinker to left field, two pitches after hitting a foul ball down the right field line.
Before losing his no-hit bid, Rasmussen had 10 strikeouts and has thrown 93 pitches, 59 for strikes through six innings.
Matt Garza is the only Tampa Bay pitcher to throw a no-hitter. Garza no-hit Detroit on July 26, 2010, at Tropicana Field.
Rasmussen ended the sixth inning by getting New York's Cody Bellinger on a flyball to right field.
Rasmussen walked Austin Wells with one out in the third and ended the inning by striking out Ben Rice on a high fastball. The 31-year-old issued a leadoff walk to Cody Bellinger and ended the fourth by striking out rookie Spencer Jones with a fastball.
Rasmussen got consecutive strikeouts on rookie George Lombard Jr. and Austin Wells to finish the fifth at 78 pitches.
The Rays can claim their fifth AL East title with a victory and took a 1-0 lead on Ryan Vilade’s groundout in the third against Max Fried. They added three in the seventh on a bunt single by Taylor Walls and a two-run base hit by Yandy Diaz.
The Yankees have been no-hit eight times. The last was a combined no-hitter by Houston’s Cristian Javier, Hector Neris and Ryan Pressly on June 25, 2022, at Yankee Stadium.

In late September, it really is another decision sitting on the manager’s desk. Clarke Schmidt has logged just two-thirds of an inning in 2026. He is active, but he has not had the time to rebuild a normal starter’s workload while Carlos Rodon, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are already taking up the big innings. item.content:encoded:
The Yankees activated Clarke Schmidt from the 60-day injured list on Sept. 16. On paper, that should read like uncomplicated good news. In late September, it really is another decision sitting on the manager’s desk.
Clarke Schmidt has logged just two-thirds of an inning in 2026. He is active, but he has not had the time to rebuild a normal starter’s workload while Carlos Rodon, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are already taking up the big innings.
Add Will Warren to that conversation and the Yankees have more options than clean answers. A talented pitcher returning late is useful. It can also make the October board much harder to read.
The Yankees cannot let sentiment choose the role
Schmidt earned real trust before the injury, which makes this harder than it would be for a fringe arm. He is not someone the Yankees should stash in the background and forget about.
But a postseason roster does not care about last spring or last year. It cares about who can get through a difficult inning right now. The Yankees need to decide whether Schmidt can help as a short reliever, a piggyback option or simply depth behind their first group of starters.
The answer does not have to be permanent this week. It does need to be honest. Trying to force a long starter’s buildup into the final days of the season would create a problem the Yankees do not need.
October will reward the Yankees for getting practical
Schmidt returning gives the Yankees an extra good pitcher. That matters. The club should enjoy having more pitching than most teams can claim this late in the year.
Still, the safest route is probably the simplest one: use him in the role his current workload supports, then see if the games demand more. The Yankees have enough established starters. What they need from Schmidt is clarity, not a rushed label.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings and the New York Yankees prevented the Tampa Bay Rays from clinching the AL East title with a 2-0 victory in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday.
The Yankees (90-66) moved six games ahead of the Red Sox for the AL's top wild-card spot. Tampa Bay (95-61) has a magic number of two to clinch the AL East for the fifth time in team history and first since 2021.
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning off Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez (15-5) and also started a key double play to end the sixth by throwing out Victor Mesa Jr. at first.
Rodón (7-3) struck out eight and walked none while completing eight innings for the first time since July 11, 2025, against the Cubs. The left-hander, who recorded his 100th win, became the 18th active pitcher to reach 1,500 career strikeouts when he fanned Jonny DeLuca on a slider for the second out of the eighth.
Rodón also struck out AL MVP candidate Junior Caminero on a slider in the dirt in the seventh with a runner on after reaching 98 mph on the previous two pitches.
Rodón threw first-pitch strikes to 15 of 25 hitters and improved to 3-1 in seven starts since returning from left elbow inflammation last month.
Following a double by Ben Rice off Martinez in the fourth, Bellinger lifted the next pitch into the right field seats for a 2-0 lead.
After a single by Mesa started the sixth, Richie Palacios lifted a fly ball to Bellinger. Bellinger made the catch and a strong one-hop throw to first baseman Luis García Jr. to easily complete the double play and get his eighth outfield assist this year.
Martinez allowed two runs and five hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out seven and lost for the first time since July 9.
David Bednar retired Yandy Díaz for his 35th save in 39 chances and finish New York's 15th shutout in 2 hours, 2 minutes - the Yankees' fastest game this season.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72 ERA) opposes New York LHP Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the second game.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees win first game of doubleheader behind Carlos Rodón’s milestone performance
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of
item.content:encoded:
The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of the day’s doubleheader, 2-0.
Rodón burst out of the gate like he had a point to prove, whiffing the first two batters of the game Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda on a pair of filthy sliders. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are likely locks for the postseason rotation, meaning if the Yankees elect to stick with a three-man unit, that final spot comes down to Rodón and Gerrit Cole. Aaron Boone has affirmed his commitment to Cole as the Game One starter in a prospective Wild Card Series. This seemingly leaves Rodón on the bubble, which might explain the extra edge he was pitching with this afternoon.
His teammates didn’t do themselves any favors early, burning both ABS challenges in the first inning. I expect the Yankees to tighten the strings on who gets to challenge and in what situation come the playoffs as you cannot deprive yourself of such a vital tool with eight innings still to play.
Martinez entered this game with the lowest walk rate of any qualified starter and among the league’s best at limiting hard contact. He was true to form going the first turn through the order without allowing a base runner. He was helped by the collectively poor approach from the lineup, with four out of the nine batters including the side in the third striking out against a pitcher with the lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters.
That started to change the second turn through the order, the Yankees finally starting to do some damage against the high volume of pitches Martinez was throwing over the heart of the plate, starting with a Ben Rice double into the corner in right to lead off the fourth. The very next pitch Martinez threw rocketed out of the yard, Cody Bellinger blasting a first pitch sinker into the seats in right for a two-run homer — his fifth homer in the last 12 games.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones singled with two outs to put runners on the corners. Jones then stole second unopposed, but Anthony Volpe struck out swinging to strand the pair in scoring position. They kept up the pressure in the fifth, José Caballero reaching on a bunt single against his former team and then stealing second and third followed by a Rice walk to put runners on the corners with one out. However, Bellinger popped out and Heliot Ramos flew out as they stranded a pair in consecutive frames.
Rodón settled into an impressive groove after a Chandler Simpson single in the second, retiring the next ten batters in order until Victor Mesa Jr. led off the sixth with a single. After Rodón whiffed Jorge Mateo on a slider for his sixth strikeout, he got Richie Palacios to line out to left. Mesa was running on the play and momentarily forget he had to sprint back to first, allowing Bellinger to throw an absolute seed to Luis García Jr., who applid the tag for the inning-ending double play.
With Rodón’s pitch count standing at just 89 after seven, Boone decided to go batter-to-batter in the eighth. However, Rodón ensured his manager had no choice to make, completing the eighth inning on just seven pitches, including the 1,500th strikeout of his career. It’s tied for his longest start as a Yankee, matching the eight innings he pitched against the Cubs on July 11, 2025.
Rodón entered this start as perhaps the Yankees’ most in-form pitcher behind Schlittler. Including today, in his last eight starts, Rodón has a 1.67 ERA while holding batters to a measly .134 batting average against. He had all his pitches working today, but this really felt like a throwback to his peak years with Chicago and San Francisco. He got whiffs in bunches on the four-seamer above the zone and slider below it. In likely his penultimate start of the regular season, Rodón dominated for eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out eight to lower his ERA to 2.67 on the year.
The Yankees didn’t manage another base runner in the final three innings, but Rodón made sure that it wouldn’t come back to haunt them. David Bednar pitched a one-two-three ninth to secure his 35th save of the season. The gap to the Rays now stands at five games as the Yankees become the second team in the AL to 90 wins. At worst, they have clinched the four seed in the AL, guaranteeing home field advantage in a prospective AL Wild Card Series.
The Yankees have a few hours’ rest before taking the field again tonight. Max Fried starts the night game of the doubleheader against Drew Rasmussen. First pitch is scheduled for 7:05 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES, so stick around!

item.content:encoded:
Carlos Rodón delivered his best starts of the season Tuesday afternoon, leading the New York Yankees to a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
Rodón allowed only three hits, all singles, while striking out eight over eight scoreless innings. It was his first eight-inning performance since July 11, 2025.
The left-hander retired 19 straight batters at one point, with two double plays helping preserve the perfect stretch. Jose Caballero started a 5-4-3 double play in the second inning, while Cody Bellinger caught a line drive in the third before throwing to first base, where Luis García Jr. tagged Victor Mesa Jr. trying to return to the bag.
Rodón also reached a career milestone in the eighth inning when he recorded his 1,500th strikeout. His season earned-run average dropped to 2.67, while he has posted a 1.42 earned-run average in four September starts.
New York’s offense struggled to generate much against Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez, who retired the Yankees in order the first time through the lineup.
That changed in the fourth inning. Ben Rice opened the frame with a double before Bellinger followed with a two-run home run to right field, giving New York its only runs of the game.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones followed with consecutive two-out singles, but Anthony Volpe struck out to end the inning.
David Bednar closed the game with a scoreless ninth for his 35th save.
The victory moved New York to within five games of Tampa Bay in the American League East.
The teams meet again Tuesday at 7:05 p.m. Max Fried starts for New York against Drew Rasmussen.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Yankees' Carlos Rodon Could Shockingly Take Gerrit Cole's Job
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: New York Yankees pitcher Carlos Rodon is making quite a case for himself. item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees pitcher Carlos Rodon is making quite a case for himself.
The general consensus is that the Yankees' No. 2 and 3 starters will be some combination of Gerrit Cole and Max Fried, although Cole's recent struggles have now put a spotlight on the evolving situation.
Carlos Rodon then intensified it with his performance on Tuesday afternoon.
In the opener of New York's four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Rodon tossed eight scoreless innings, registering nine strikeouts while allowing just three hits. He also didn't issue a single walk.
Quietly, Rodon has been enjoying a tremendous season, perhaps his best as a Yankee.
Yes, Rodon's 2026 campaign has been abbreviated, as he began the year on the shelf due to offseason elbow surgery and then missed some more time as a result of an elbow issue midway through the year, but in the 16 games he has pitched, Rodon owns a 2.67 ERA and 1.06 WHIP while averaging 9.7 strikeouts per nine innings.
What's more, Rodon has surrendered just two runs or less in each of his last eight starts, and he has allowed one run or less in six of them.
So has Rodon now entered the conversation as a potential No. 2 or 3 starter in the Yankees' postseason rotation? And could Cole get the boot?
Cole pitched considerably better in his last outing, giving up just two runs in six innings. However, his swing-and-miss stuff still wasn't there, and it's hard to ignore just how home-run prone he has been over the last month.
Chances are, Boone will give Cole the nod based on reputation and seniority alone, but let's say the 36-year-old has another middling start this week. Then what?
At that point, Boone would have to seriously consider giving Rodon the nod. The left-hander has flown under the radar in recent weeks, but he has truly been outstanding.
It sounds unheard of to remove Cole from the top three of the Yankees' playoff rotation. But results matter, and Cole has not produced a whole lot of positive ones recently.
We'll see if Boone ultimately makes what would be a surprising decision for the postseason.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Carlos Rodón dominates as Yankees beat Rays in first game of doubleheader, keep AL East dreams alive
item.dc:creator: Peter Sblendorio
item.description: Given the depth of the Yankees’ rotation, there’s a strong possibility — perhaps even a likelihood — that Carlos Rodón won’t be asked to start a game in the best-of-three Wild Card round of the playoffs.T But Rodón looked every bit of an ace in Tuesday afternoon’s 2-0 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to kick off a doubleheader in the Bronx — a victory that kept the Yankees’ dreams of a division crown alive for at least a little while longer. Rodón hurled a season-high eight innings, striking out eigh
item.content:encoded:
Given the depth of the Yankees’ rotation, there’s a strong possibility — perhaps even a likelihood — that Carlos Rodón won’t be asked to start a game in the best-of-three Wild Card round of the playoffs.T
But Rodón looked every bit of an ace in Tuesday afternoon’s 2-0 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to kick off a doubleheader in the Bronx — a victory that kept the Yankees’ dreams of a division crown alive for at least a little while longer.
Rodón hurled a season-high eight innings, striking out eight while limiting the Rays to three hits (all singles) without issuing a walk.
An eighth-inning strikeout of Jonny DeLuca was the 1,500th of Rodón’s 12-year career. Two pitches later, Rodón induced a soft groundout by Victor Mesa Jr. to end the inning, then walked off the mound to a standing ovation.
With the win — the 100th of his career — Rodón improved to 7-3 with a 2.67 ERA. A two-run home run by Cody Bellinger against Nick Martinez in the fourth inning provided all the run support Rodón would need.
It was the 26th start in a row in which Rodón limited an opponent to three runs or fewer, extending a franchise record.
Offseason elbow surgery delayed Rodón’s season debut until May 10, and he missed more than a month over the summer due to left elbow inflammation.
That’s limited Rodón to only 16 starts this season, and before Tuesday, he had not pitched more than 6.1 innings in any of them.
But Rodón has been consistently sharp over his 84.1 innings, and he’s pitching better than ever as the postseason approaches.
Whether Rodón actually gets to make a playoff start, however, may depend on whether the Yankees advance to the ALDS.
By winning game one of Tuesday’s doubleheader, the Yankees cut their deficit in the AL East to five games with six to play. But they began the day knowing they would need to sweep the division-leading Rays in this week’s four-game series to keep that goal alive.
Cam Schlittler is guaranteed to start a Wild Card game for the Yankees, while manager Aaron Boone said last week that he expects Gerrit Cole to start one, too.
That would leave one more game for either Rodón or Max Fried, who entered Tuesday’s nightcap with a 5-4 record and a 2.63 ERA.
In six playoff starts with the Yankees, Rodón is 1-2 with a 6.92 ERA.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Rays, Yankees each face clinching scenarios in doubleheader
item.dc:creator: This article first appeared; Was Syndicated
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday. With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener. Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox. The Ray
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener.
Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rays, who are seeking their fifth division title, have led the AL East every day since June 27.
Following a 2-7 run last month, Tampa Bay is 19-7 since Aug. 23 and just went 8-1 on a homestand against the Houston Astros, Athletics and Red Sox. It featured three walk-off wins and ended with Sunday's 5-1 win over Boston which saw Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca drive in two runs apiece.
"We knew what we had to do," Tampa Bay pitcher Griffin Jax said. "We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier."
The Yankees play host to the Rays for the first time since Aaron Judge's game-ending two-run homer for a 2-0 victory May 24. Judge returned Sept. 8 after missing 84 games with a fractured rib, played seven games and returned to the injured list with a strained calf.
The Yankees are 48-41 in games Judge has not played and enter the upcoming series after losing two of three at Arizona, including an 8-4 loss Sunday. Rookies George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones hit two of New York's three home runs in the third inning, but Brent Headrick gave up a grand slam to Arizona's Nolan Arenado in the fifth.
"We're going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday, and then we'll keep going from there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "We've been through a lot as a team this year already, and we've answered the bell at the turns. We're looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason."
Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94 ERA) will start the opener for Tampa Bay followed by Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) in the second game. Martinez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA in his past five starts and 2-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Yankees.
Since allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings at home against the Yankees on July 9, Rasmussen is 8-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past 11 starts. He is 4-2 with a 1.87 ERA in 10 career outings against the Yankees.
New York will start Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95) in the opener followed by Max Fried (5-4, 2.63).
Rodon is 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 18 and is 3-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 10 career starts against the Rays
Fried is 1-0 with a 1.83 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 29 and allowed one run in seven innings last Tuesday at Minnesota. He is 5-0 with a 1.26 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.
